_comment: Single source of truth for material that must NEVER be committed to this repository. Read by scripts/check-private-paths.js (the CI gate) and pinned by scripts/__tests__/private-paths.test.ts. Every entry is a third party's property in some form. Adding a path here is cheap; discovering one after a publish is not. NOTE ON WORDING: these descriptions are deliberately non-specific, because this file is public and an inventory that catalogues what it is protecting is itself a map to it. Say what an agent needs in order to classify a new file and refuse to commit it, and no more. The full detail is in the archived private repository. Do not restore it here, and do not reproduce it in a commit message, a code comment, a PR body or a summary of this list.

_kinds.vendor-binary: A third party's compiled or serialised artefacts. Not regenerable from this repository.
_kinds.vendor-source: A third party's own code, in any recovered form.
_kinds.vendor-notes: Our written analysis of the above. Publishing the analysis publishes the substance even when the payload itself is gone.
_kinds.vendor-procedure: Provenance notes. The most sensitive category and the one to be strictest about, because it is of use to a reader who holds none of the rest. Never quote or paraphrase its contents anywhere.

_archive.bucket: Upload to the object-storage bucket (see scripts/upload-model-assets.js) before removing from the tree. Not recoverable from this repository once deleted and not regenerable here, so the upload is a prerequisite rather than a formality.
_archive.runtime-fetch: Already served from object storage at runtime; the tree copy was a fallback and is gone.

paths.reason: Third-party artefacts with no loader — archival only, nothing read them at runtime. Not regenerable from this repository, so removing them was a one-way door and re-committing them is never the answer.

Third-party artefacts the runtime loads. They come from object storage, there is no tree copy behind that any more, and the boot check fails production rather than quietly serving a degraded result. The exclusion is our own recorded test vectors, which are ours and stay public.

Third-party values, read at runtime from a directory delivered at boot rather than imported at build time — which is what let them stop being a repository dependency at all. The exclusions are our own code only: the loader, the type declarations that describe a format rather than any values, the tests and the README. One table the device needs is served from an authenticated route rather than bundled into the client.
A third party's own code in recovered form, with our notes on it. Referenced only from code comments and never imported, which is what made it removable with no code change.
A second copy of the same, kept beside the tooling that produced it. Referenced only from code comments, never imported.
Our written analysis of the material above. Written from it, so publishing this would publish the substance even once the payload itself is gone.

The single most sensitive file that was ever in this repository. Its parked section is provenance detail of the kind the vendor-procedure note above describes. Do not restore it, and do not describe its contents anywhere — including in a summary of why it is on this list.
Provenance record for the bundle, carrying third-party identifiers and hashes that should not be public. Same handling as the entry above.
An index of the whole archive — what exists and where each part of it lives. Useful precisely to the extent that it maps material that must not be public, which is the reason it cannot be.

Our protocol knowledge base for the direct-Bluetooth pipeline. Owner decision, 2026-08-10: the port itself stays public — it is our own code and structurally cannot be split out — but the write-up does not. Be clear-eyed about what that buys. It raises the effort to reproduce the work; it does not make the subject unknowable from the published code, and nobody should plan as though it did.
